structure.heading: Milestone Delivery Health and Next-Period Commitments (Reporting Period Ending 30 Jun 2026)
text_content: **Milestone Delivery Health and Next-Period Commitments (Reporting Period Ending 30 Jun 2026)**

As of 30 Jun 2026 the Programme milestone health shows 18 of 24 milestones are Green (75.0%), 4 are Amber (16.7%), and 2 are Red (8.3%). The Programme Office notes a net improvement of two Green milestones since the prior reporting period, driven by accelerated testing and supplier remediation work managed by the Delivery Unit. Remaining Amber items are concentrated in Integration and Training streams; Red items relate to vendor performance and a key regulatory dependency. Current trajectory indicates the critical path remains constrained but manageable, with contingency reserves available at stream level and trigger points defined for escalation to the Steering Committee.
no‑go decision by the Steering Committee.

For 01 Jul–31 Jul 2026 the programme commits to complete 6 milestones, including Data Migration Dress Rehearsal by 22 Jul 2026. Delivery Unit and Data & Infrastructure teams are accountable; progress will be reported weekly to the Programme Director and sponsors. Acceptance criteria for each July milestone are defined, dependencies logged, and resource allocations baselined to ensure the Wave 1 critical path is protected.

structure.heading: Budget-at-Completion Forecast, Dependency Risks, and Steering Committee Escalations
text_content: **Budget-at-Completion Forecast, Dependency Risks, and Steering Committee Escalations**

The current budget position shows a Budget at Completion (BAC) of $120.0m and an Estimate at Completion (EAC) of $128.5m, a +$8.5m variance (≈+7.1%). Drivers include scope growth from late change requests, vendor change orders, accelerated contractor rates, and drawdown of risk reserves for remediation. The programme proposes mitigations—scope deferrals, vendor negotiation, and targeted contingency release—but until a Steering Committee decision is made the EAC remains $128.5m. Financial controls will be tightened with weekly reforecasting and a temporary hold on non-critical spend pending the 10 Jul 2026 committee meeting.

There are five high‑severity dependency risks requiring active management. Critical items include: (1) vendor API delivery currently forecast for 29 Jul 2026 that would impact Wave 1 Go‑Live on 15 Aug 2026; (2) constrained data migration windows due to business blackout periods; (3) third‑party payment gateway certification; (4) cloud tenancy provisioning lag; and (5) limited specialist integration resource availability in September. Each dependency has an owner, assessed impact, and mitigation options; the vendor API is on the critical path and is tracked daily with the supplier.

Two decisions are escalated to the Steering Committee for 10 Jul 2026: approve a $3.0m contingency release and approve a 4‑week schedule change request for CRM integration. Approval of the $3.0m reduces the forecast variance from +$8.5m to +$5.5m and lowers the EAC to $125.5m; refusal requires further scope deferrals and tighter expenditure controls. The 4‑week CRM change will reduce integration risk and deconflict downstream testing but may shift dependent milestones. The programme recommends concurrent approval of both items to stabilise the schedule and materially reduce financial exposure and protect stakeholder commitments.

sections.heading: Milestone Health and Progress
sections.body: Customer Portal Release 2 entered user acceptance testing on 18 April 2026 and is tracking to complete by 20 May, with defect density trending 12% below the prior release baseline. Finance Process Standardisation has completed design sign-off across all regions, with deployment commencing in the EMEA cluster on 9 May. Infrastructure Modernisation has achieved 70% server decommissioning, though final cutover is contingent on network resilience testing scheduled for mid-May. The integrated readiness review conducted on 29 April confirmed that cross-workstream alignment remains effective but time-sensitive.

sections.heading: Financial Position and Forecast
sections.body: Year-to-date expenditure stands at $48.7m against an approved budget of $51.2m, reflecting a favourable variance of $2.5m primarily driven by deferred vendor invoices. However, the latest Estimate at Completion (EAC) projects a Budget-at-Completion of $104.6m against the approved $101.8m baseline. The forecast overrun of $2.8m is attributable to extended contractor support for data remediation and increased cloud hosting costs during dual-run operations. Mitigation options, including scope re-phasing and internal resource substitution, are being assessed.

sections.heading: Dependency Risks and Escalations
sections.body: The primary cross-workstream risk concerns the dependency between Data Migration Phase II and the Infrastructure capacity uplift, with a two-week buffer remaining before critical path impact. Additionally, alignment with the Enterprise Cybersecurity uplift programme is required to finalise identity federation controls prior to go-live. Two escalations require Steering Committee decision: approval of a $1.4m contingency drawdown to secure additional migration tooling, and confirmation of a revised sequencing approach that advances regional deployment in APAC ahead of North America. Timely decisions are required by 13 May to avoid schedule compression.

sections.heading: Next-Period Commitments
sections.body: For the reporting period 5 May to 2 June 2026, the programme commits to completing user acceptance testing for Portal Release 2, finalising infrastructure resilience certification, and executing the first regional deployment of standardised finance processes. A consolidated benefits tracking update will be presented at the June Steering Committee, incorporating validated cost-to-serve reductions from the pilot region. The programme team will also deliver a refined cost containment plan to address the projected EAC variance.

Section Milestone Health and Progress
Customer Portal Release 2 entered user acceptance testing on 18 April 2026 and is tracking to complete by 20 May, with defect density trending 12% below the prior release baseline. Finance Process Standardisation has completed design sign-off across all regions, with deployment commencing in the EMEA cluster on 9 May. Infrastructure Modernisation has achieved 70% server decommissioning, though final cutover is contingent on network resilience testing scheduled for mid-May. The integrated readiness review conducted on 29 April confirmed that cross-workstream alignment remains effective but time-sensitive.

Section Financial Position and Forecast
Year-to-date expenditure stands at $48.7m against an approved budget of $51.2m, reflecting a favourable variance of $2.5m primarily driven by deferred vendor invoices. However, the latest Estimate at Completion (EAC) projects a Budget-at-Completion of $104.6m against the approved $101.8m baseline. The forecast overrun of $2.8m is attributable to extended contractor support for data remediation and increased cloud hosting costs during dual-run operations. Mitigation options, including scope re-phasing and internal resource substitution, are being assessed.

Section Dependency Risks and Escalations
The primary cross-workstream risk concerns the dependency between Data Migration Phase II and the Infrastructure capacity uplift, with a two-week buffer remaining before critical path impact. Additionally, alignment with the Enterprise Cybersecurity uplift programme is required to finalise identity federation controls prior to go-live. Two escalations require Steering Committee decision: approval of a $1.4m contingency drawdown to secure additional migration tooling, and confirmation of a revised sequencing approach that advances regional deployment in APAC ahead of North America. Timely decisions are required by 13 May to avoid schedule compression.

Section Next-Period Commitments
For the reporting period 5 May to 2 June 2026, the programme commits to completing user acceptance testing for Portal Release 2, finalising infrastructure resilience certification, and executing the first regional deployment of standardised finance processes. A consolidated benefits tracking update will be presented at the June Steering Committee, incorporating validated cost-to-serve reductions from the pilot region. The programme team will also deliver a refined cost containment plan to address the projected EAC variance.
